findings.where: Hero, the 'Get in touch' button; the nav's 'Contact' link; the page end, which has no footer
findings.fault: The page never shows Mark's email address. The only way to contact him is a button that quietly opens the visitor's mail app (mailto:). Its arrow suggests it leads to another page. The nav's 'Contact' points to '#', and there is no footer with the address as link text.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer on a locked-down work laptop that uses webmail. Clicking does nothing or opens an unconfigured mail client, and there is no address to copy. The one action the site exists for fails for exactly the audience it serves (first-visit trust item 7).

findings.where: Hero, the standfirst's last sentence, 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience'
findings.fault: The first screen claims standing with a size word: years counted, not work shown. This is the exact example the house's 'feel the CV' rule bans, and it is the boastful note the brief's 'one strong line, no boasts' rules out. The World Bank credential before it already does the job by being checkable.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who selects consultants against terms of reference. They discount adjectives and counts and look for named bodies and roles. Mark has also asked for confidence without big-firm claims (client value 6).

findings.where: Article specimen, the blue italic pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…')
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in logo blue, which the tile's own palette reserves for the wordmark, links and the button. Static text that a reader cannot click takes the link colour. On a real article it sits a few lines from real blue links.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article, who reads blue text as clickable and taps the quote. Angélique too: she will copy the pattern when she adds posts, so 'blue means link' stops holding across the site.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the principle words 'precise, light, quick' and the timeline (heading lines rising in 500 ms, 580 ms total)
findings.fault: The motion character is brisk UI motion applied to the headline. The brief asks for 'calm first', a quiet moment before any text asks for anything, and 'smooth animation built around the aqueduct'. 'Quick' and a headline popping up at 0 ms set the opposite tone, and the sketch never moves the mark.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for a calm opening and smooth, aqueduct-led motion and dislikes busyness. The animation round (#9) would inherit a principle that pulls against his brief.

findings.where: Type pair (desktop): 'Gelasio' in the left column and 'Source Sans 3' in the right column, under one 'Type pair' label
findings.fault: The pair is split across the column gutter, and the right half sits in the column that holds 'Texture' above and 'Motion sketch' below. Read down that column, 'Source Sans 3' looks like a separate, unlabelled section, not half of a pair.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or the layout-round designer, reading the tile. They have to work out which label the sans specimen belongs to, and the two faces are not seen side by side as a pair.

findings.where: Style-tile section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' have a hairline rule under them; 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' do not
findings.fault: Like section headings are treated differently, with no reason the reader can see.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader of the tile, or the next designer, who will wonder whether the rule means something and copy the inconsistency into the layout round.

findings.fault: It is set as a display heading in Source Sans 3, though the tile's own type pair says the sans is for 'the nav, buttons, labels and dates only' and Gelasio does display. The tile breaks its own rule.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer, who must draw inside the tile's type rules and here finds two answers to the same question.

findings.fault: A button that replays the animation is dressed as a prose link (blue, underlined). It takes the link's reserved underline.
findings.who_objects: A keyboard or screen-magnifier user who expects an underlined blue word to go somewhere and gets an in-place replay instead. The tile would also teach the layout round that underlined text can be a button.

findings.where: Phone hero, the portrait stand-in block below 'Get in touch'
findings.fault: The block starts about 108 px from the left edge and runs flush to the right. Its left edge lines up with nothing above it, so the column looks misaligned rather than deliberately bleeding off the edge.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor, most often arriving from a LinkedIn link. The stray indent reads as a layout slip just where Mark's portrait will stand.

findings.where: Hero and the page as a whole
findings.fault: Apart from one credential, the page shows no third-party evidence of work (no work rows, no named bodies, nothing hosted by an outside body). The one dated lecture appears only as a link at the foot of the article specimen.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency reader who has to be sure Mark has done this kind of work for organisations like theirs before writing to him (first-visit trust items 3 and 14).
